subject: MSA + Order Form: governing law, forum, and injunctive relief - redline request
content:
From: Sasha Levin <sasha@summitbridge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Miller <emiller@gc-lawfirm.com>; legal@summitbridge.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: governing law, forum, and injunctive relief - redline request

Jordan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, SummitBridge's GC has asked us to propose specific language around choice of law and an injunctive-relief carveout that preserves court access in the event of IP/data confidentiality issues. Attached are: our current redlines to the MSA, a short matrix that sketches preferred forum priority, and an annotated Order Form with the clause placement.

High-level asks:
- Can Redwood confirm whether you can accept a split approach: Delaware law for contract interpretation but the right to seek emergency injunctive relief in state or federal court in SummitBridge's headquarters (NY)?
- If Redwood cannot accept NY for injunctive relief, will you accept a carveout that permits emergency relief in either party's domicile or the place where the infringement is occurring?
- Any operational impacts we should expect if Redwood adds a limited court-access carveout (routing, SLA exceptions, legal ops involvement)?

Attachments: Draft_MSA_redlines_v3.docx (docx), injunction_fallback_matrix.xlsx (xls/x), OrderForm_v2-markup.pdf (pdf)

Happy to jump on a quick sync if that helps.

—Sasha
Sasha Levin
Head of Partnerships | SummitBridge
[sent from mobile]

-----Original Message-----

>
> Sasha —
>
> Appreciate the clear asks and the attachments. Quick notes from product/ops side before legal weighs in:
> - Operationally, a narrow injunctive carveout for emergency data preservation is workable but we need to define the trigger events precisely (e.g., imminent exfiltration, compromise of secret key material used for customer data).
> - If an out-of-region court access is allowed as an exception, we may need a documented escalation path so requests to pause or divert traffic are processed under a defined SLO and logged for compliance.
>
> Looping in Kimberly + David to propose legal language.
>
> Best,
> Jordan Blake
> Director, Commercial | Redwood Inference
>
> [attachment: injunction_fallback_matrix.xlsx]
>

On Mon, Jul 14, 2025 at 11:05 AM Evelyn Miller <emiller@gc-lawfirm.com> wrote:

> From: Evelyn Miller <emiller@gc-lawfirm.com>
> To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.com
> Cc: Sasha Levin <sasha@summitbridge.com>; marissa.cole@redwood.com
> Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 11:05:12 -0400
> Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: governing law, forum, and injunctive relief - redline request
>
> Jordan/Kimberly —
>
> Per SummitBridge's instruction: they prefer Delaware law for contract interpretation but need a guaranteed mechanism to seek emergency injunctive relief in NY courts for expedited preservation orders. Their position is narrow — not a general waiver of Redwood's forum selection.
>
> Suggested approach for consideration:
> 1) Governing law: Delaware (explicit).
> 2) Dispute resolution: binding arbitration for covered monetary disputes (single arbitrator, AAA rules) with a carveout for interim equitable relief.
> 3) Injunctive relief carveout: either party may seek provisional or injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction to preserve rights relating to (i) alleged misappropriation of Confidential Information or (ii) unauthorized access to Production data; such request shall not be deemed a waiver of the agreement's arbitration clause for other disputes.
>
> If Redwood is comfortable with that language, we can propose a short redline that preserves Delaware law + the emergency relief carveout.
>
> Best,
> Evelyn Miller
> Partner, GC Law Firm (on behalf of SummitBridge)
>
> [attachment: OrderForm_v2-markup.pdf]

-----Original Message-----
On Mon, Jul 14, 2025 at 13:30 Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:

> From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
> To: kimberly.park@redwood.com; david.kim@redwood.com; marissa.cole@redwood.com
> Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 13:30:05 -0400
> Subject: Redwood internal: SummitBridge redline — quick proposal
>
> Team —
>
> I drafted the below proposal to circulate back to SummitBridge (short, lawyer-friendly). Kimberly, can you weigh in on the exact phrasing? David/Marissa, call out any ops/SLA items we should flag back to them as non-starters.
>
> Proposed short language to include in MSA (for legal redline):
> "Governing Law; Emergency Equitable Relief. This Agreement will be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to conflict of law rules. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek provisional, injunctive or other equitable relief in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction to prevent the actual or threatened misappropriation of trade secrets, unauthorized access to customer production data, or other circumstances in which irreparable harm may occur. An application for such interim relief shall not constitute a waiver of the Agreement's arbitration provisions for disputes otherwise subject to arbitration."
>
> Operational notes to surface if we accept:
> - We should accept injunctive carveout but require a notice-and-response window of 24 hours where feasible (except in extraordinary emergency).
> - For emergency preservation orders that require immediate traffic/persistence changes, we will create a runbook to be executed with SummitBridge's legal counsel sign-off.
>
> Can Kimberly prepare redline text and also flag whether the proposed 24-hour notice (best-effort) is a material concession?
>
> Thanks,
> Jordan
>
>
-----Original Message-----
On Mon, Jul 14, 2025 at 15:12 Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com> wrote:

> From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
> To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
> Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 15:12:43 -0400
> Subject: Re: Redwood internal: SummitBridge redline — quick proposal
>
> Jordan —
>
> Thanks for the draft. I like the structure. A few suggested edits so the redline is defensible:
> - Replace "without regard to conflict of law rules" with "excluding its choice-of-law rules" (standard boilerplate).
> - Add specificity to the injunctive carveout triggers so it reads: "(i) actual or threatened misappropriation of trade secrets; (ii) unauthorized access to or exfiltration of Customer Production Data; or (iii) disclosure of Confidential Information constituting a material breach that is likely to result in irreparable harm."
> - Preserve arbitration for monetary relief and add sentence: "Any application for interim equitable relief shall be without prejudice to the right of the parties to submit the underlying dispute to arbitration as provided herein."
> - Regarding the 24-hour notice: we should avoid hard-coded timelines that create performance obligations. Recommend "reasonable advance notice where feasible; in cases of immediate risk, emergency measures may be taken without prior notice followed by prompt notice to the other party."
>
> I will produce a tracked redline of the MSA and a companion snippet for the Order Form. I don't view Delaware law + injunctive carveout as a material business concession so long as (a) injunctive relief is limited to the triggers above and (b) the clause explicitly states that seeking interim relief does not waive arbitration rights.
>
> Draft deliverables by EOD today.
>
> Kimberly Park
> Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
> [attachment: Draft_MSA_redlines_v3.docx]
>
>

We'll avoid hard timelines but propose a "reasonable advance notice where feasible" baseline.
>
> We will send the redline and a one-page operational runbook for emergency preservation flows (roles, expected response times, and contact matrix) by EOD. In the meantime, attaching the matrix SummitBridge sent for our reference.
>
> Best,
> Jordan
> Director, Commercial | Redwood Inference
>
